nodes.label: Phase 1 Slice 4 — Derive Less, and Track Use
nodes.rationale: Ingest stops producing three quarters of what it produces today, and the system starts recording when a blob was last touched. No new dependencies. Its own baseline line tells the reader to check cargo for the current test count rather than trusting the document — a stale baseline is how a task convinces itself it broke nothing.

nodes.label: Derive On Demand
nodes.rationale: Ingest asks for L0 only, plus a thumbnail when the library wants one; a derive job kind asks for exactly one thing against one revision, so L1 and L2 arrive when something wants them. Targets ~665 MB to ~48 MB of derivatives per 1,000 parts. Safe because content addressing makes re-derivation byte-identical, and because a part with no thumbnail still appears in the grid.

nodes.label: KernelParams.produce
nodes.rationale: A list of what this call must make, so the kernel builds what the caller asked for and nothing else. KernelOutput.tessellations becomes a Vec and cluster.rs's ladder() is deleted. The whole rung-filing behaviour rests on one test, recorded as concentration risk rather than a defect.

nodes.label: library.auto_thumbnail
nodes.rationale: A per-library setting, default on, added by migration 0005 alongside widening the outcome CHECK to accept 'rendered'. Migration 0005 removes no row. The UI toggle renders indeterminate and disabled before its GET resolves rather than showing a confident 'on' that flips.

nodes.label: JobPayload
nodes.rationale: A typed payload discriminated by the existing job.kind COLUMN rather than serde's tag attribute, so every pre-existing {"path": ...} row still deserialises. The old untyped path had a worse failure than a bad message: payload.get("path") succeeds on any ingest-shaped payload, so an unknown kind fell through to a file read, returned Transient, and the queue retried a job it could never run three times before failing.

nodes.label: blob.last_accessed_at
nodes.rationale: The column existed since migration 0002 and nothing wrote it, yet every storage feature after this depends on it. Written by the blob route only, never in the handler — a sweep touching blobs would mark everything warm and destroy the signal. Measured proof: exactly 2 of 301 rows carried a timestamp after the exit run, the two rungs actually fetched.
